column1: # review-tiers.tsv — the ONE path-glob -> review-tier list. Both the dispatch
# step (which model a lane runs on) and the review step (who must review it)
# read this file; no second list exists anywhere. Doctrine:
#   1 = security, enforcement, gates, hooks, settings, install, auth,
#       migrations, CODEOWNERS, merge-ready logic, data-loss paths (skill prose
#       and evals are NOT here: CI on the exact sha is their gate). Strongest allowed model
#       (`Model: opus` trailer) AND an independent reviewer
#       (`Reviewed-By:` trailer naming someone other than the author).
#   2 = feature code, skill prose and evals (also the default for any unmatched path).
#   3 = docs outside the skill and hook directories. Self-review allowed.
# Matching: Python fnmatch on the repo-relative path AND on that path with a
# leading `/`, where `*` also crosses `/` — so `*/auth/*` matches both
# `src/auth/x.py` and a root-level `auth/x.py`. Anchor short words to a
# does not catch `author`, and `merge` does not catch `emergency`. A path
# matching several rows takes the STRICTEST (lowest) tier, except a PINNED row
# (tier written `2!`/`1!`) which wins outright over unpinned rows (the strictest
# pinned row wins among pins), so `references/merge-ops.md` stays tier 2 even though
# `*/merge*` matches it, and a nested `evals/scripts/gate.py` stays tier 1. Copy this file into
# a target repo and tune the globs there; keep the tier numbers' meaning.
